chunks: From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"No servant of God's prayer is accepted for forty mornings if he drinks the intoxicant, and if he dies within the forty days, he dies a death of ignorance, and if he repents, God repents to him."

key_terms.تَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ: God repented to him (accepted his repentance)
key_terms.مِيتَةً جَاهِلِيَّةًا: A death of ignorance (pre-Islamic state of disbelief/ignorance)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the acceptance of prayer for someone who drinks intoxicants?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the severe spiritual consequence of consuming *khamr*, linking it to a temporary suspension of prayer acceptance for forty days—a period often associated with the duration of major sins' impact. The mention of dying in a state of *jahiliyyah* (pre-Islamic ignorance) highlights the regression of spiritual status, while the assurance of divine acceptance upon repentance reflects the Shia emphasis on God's mercy even after grave transgressions.
